messages.body_plain:
Simon Urbanek wrote:
> Gérard,
> 
> rJava is compiling fine, it is JRI that is causing trouble and the 
> reason is that JRI is compiled independently of R, so it's not using R's 
> linker settings. A 'hot fix' is to edit rJava/jri/configure lines 
> 3329-3331 and replace
> 
> CPICF=-fPIC
> JNISO=.so
> JNILD="-shared ${JAVA_LIBS}"
> 
> by
> 
> CPICF=-KPIC
> JNISO=.so
> JNILD="-G ${JAVA_LIBS}"
> 

great, it works well with your modifs.
To install, i did:
ultra20-root% /usr/local/R-2.4.1/bin/R CMD INSTALL rJava_0.4-7.tar.gz

> I'll see if I can automate this by using R's settings for future 
> releases ...
> 
> If you still run into trouble, you may also want to add -D_REENTRANT to 
> CFLAGS and -lpthread (or analogous for your platform) to LDFLAGS if the 
> Java you link to uses native threads.
> 
no need to add these flags.

thanks for your help,

Knut,

please make sure you have configured R with Java support. If in  
doubt, run
R CMD javareconf
as root.

Also make sure you have Java from Sun and not some packaged version -  
those tend to be broken sometimes. Also if you have 64-bit Linux, you  
have to use Java 1.6 or higher. If that still doesn't help, please  
send me exactly what system you have (architecture, system version, R  
version, whether it is cran/dpkg binary etc.).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Workaround for error export: 41: stats, : bad variable name
messages.subject_clean: Workaround for error export: 41: stats, : bad variable name
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

A few people have reported the dreaded error since JGR 1.4-11 or -12  
in Linux installations (usually Ubuntu running Sun Java 1.4, 1.5, or  
1.6)

export: 41: stats,: bad variable name

Some reports indicate deleting .JGRprefsrc will prevent the error, but  
you lose your preferences.

I have a temporary workaround as well.

1. Edit .JGRprefsrc and delete the extra spaces from line 12

<entry key="DefaultPackages" value="utils, stats, rJava, methods, JGR,  
JavaGD, graphics, datasets, base"/>

to the following:

             <entry key="DefaultPackages"  
value="utils,stats,rJava,methods,JGR,JavaGD,graphics,datasets,base"/>

2. Then remove write permissions to .JGRprefsrc

chmod ugo-w .JGRprefsrc

3. Run JGR either from within R or via the run script
A. > library(JGR)
    > JGR()
B. /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/JGR/cont/run

You may need to run 3A first as root to create the run script, and  
then change the execute privileges for the run script.

Hope this helps with this bug.

Bing

Judging by the error messages you are apparently running R in a  
German locale. Setting LC_NUMERIC to a German locale does exactly  
what you describe, because in German locale "," is the decimal point  
separator (as opposed to "." in English locales). You may want to set  
LC_NUMERIC to "C" in order to get the more common behavior.

(As a side note, someone should fix the German translation of R  
messages, they are indeed quite funny as you will find out when using  
Sys.setlocale("LC_NUMERIC","C") :P )

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Richard,

the eval command parses the passed string, evaluates the resulting  
expression and returns the result. I'll look into 1 which is probably  
caused by the fact that it evaluates to no expression (it should  
return an error instead of crashing). 2 and 3 are clearly results as  
expected, because "c(1," is no valid R expression and neither is ", 
2)" nor "f=function(arg) {".

Again, recall that you are not dealing with R command line here.  
Although you didn't tell us what you are doing, it appears as if you  
are trying to parse some R code line-by-line which is not how R  
parser works - you have to parse the entire expression, not just  
parts of it. You should either use the corresponding function in R  
(e.g. source) or if you want a real console, you should use the  
console callbacks (e.g. rReadConsole etc.).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Today I tried out the Cairo package for R. It looks really nice!

I have two points I wanted to give feedback to:

First, the compile process: configure aborted at the first time,
complaining about missing cairo.h. So I installed libcairo2-dev (on
Ubuntu Feisty). But then during compilation, a missing Intrinsic.h
stopped the compilation. On Ubuntu (and probably on Debian, too), it's
in libxt-dev, installing that made the installation work. 
I guess configure should look for Intrinsic.h as well.

Second, SVG output. The anti-aliased PNG graphics look really sweet, and
are much better than R's default PNGs. But I was initially looking for
SVG output. I don't have an CairoSVG()-device after installation.
Cairo(file="test.svg", type="svg", units="pt") generates an SVG file,
but it doesn't contain the plot as SVG shapes, but only containes a
base64-encoded embedded PNG-image. And this seems to be empty, too, as
neither rsvg, nor Inkscape, nor Batik display any plot.

Am I missing something? Is Ubuntu's cairo-version to blame? Or do I need
another library at compile time?

Thanks,
Frederik



-- 
Frederik Elwert

Fachbereich Sozialwissenschaften

purposes it doesn't) so the map format is sufficient so far.
